options: Only when no exception was thrown
Only when an exception was thrown and caught
Always — whether the try block succeeded, threw a caught exception, or is about to return
Only if you explicitly call it
questions.explain: finally always executes before control leaves the try/catch structure, regardless of what happened in try or catch.

questions.q: Which exception is most commonly thrown by assigning a SOQL query to a singleton sObject variable that returns zero or multiple rows?
options: DmlException
QueryException
ListException
NullPointerException
questions.explain: QueryException covers SOQL problems, including a singleton assignment that doesn't get exactly one row.

options: The total number of DML statements executed in the transaction
The number of records that failed within that DML operation
The number of fields affected by the error
The maximum DML statements allowed per transaction
questions.explain: getNumDml() reports how many records in the bulk DML operation failed.

questions.q: Why does `catch (Exception e)` also catch a `DmlException`?
options: It doesn't — DmlException must have its own catch block
Because all built-in and custom exception types extend the base Exception class
Because Apex automatically converts DmlException to Exception at runtime
Only if allOrNone is set to false
questions.explain: Every exception type, built-in or custom, ultimately extends Exception, so a catch block for Exception matches any exception type.

questions.q: When listing multiple catch blocks for related exception types, what order should they go in?
options: Alphabetical order by exception name
Least specific (e.g. Exception) first, most specific last
Most specific type first, with a generic Exception catch-all last
Order doesn't matter in Apex
questions.explain: Apex checks catch blocks top to bottom and uses the first match, so specific types must come before a generic catch-all or the specific block would never be reached.
